blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 28 in June to 27 in September (−3.6%), and it took 4.2% of the city’s 215 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 18 in June to 30 in September (+66.7%), and it took 5.3% of the city’s 318 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Poplar for detached houses in July, August, September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, September (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default — and effectively the only — land form: A bare lot sold in either fabric is a fee-simple parcel: the buyer's own title, no strata corporation, no strata fee and no Form B.

Lot character, as the research states it: urban minimums are set by the RS zones — RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m² and RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m² in City rezoning reports applying Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014; rural A1 land subdivides at a minimum of 8.0 ha. These are subdivision minimums, not measured sizes and not a promise any specific lot can be split — a lot already at or near its zone minimum has no subdivision room.
Bare-land strata: none verified in Poplar

Serviced vs unserviced ground — the north/south split is the point: urban north lots sit in the City's serviced subdivision fabric (parcel-level connection status still confirmed with the City). Lots at the rural south edge may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite systems must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation through Fraser Health. Never assume south-edge servicing matches King Road servicing.

ALR vs non-ALR split: rural lots at the south edge toward Huntingdon Road are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve; no Poplar-wide ALR percentage is published, so no split figure is stated — status is parcel-by-parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder, and where the A1 zone applies the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 ha.

Drainage/flood character: Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system; the City describes Sumas Prairie as a low-lying agricultural area subject to Nooksack River overflow flooding. That description is for Sumas Prairie to the east/southeast — a floodplain finding for a single Poplar lot is UNVERIFIED and must be checked against Zoning Bylaw Schedule E Floodplain Boundaries in the City WebMap.

Airport diligence: Poplar is east of Abbotsford International Airport (YXX); where a lot falls inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500, AZR height limits (approach, outer and transitional surfaces) and NAV CANADA / Transport Canada approvals apply before a City permit. Whether any single lot is inside that area: UNCONFIRMED parcel by parcel.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Poplar

items.t: The City of Abbotsford's own demographic profile name for the same ground is "South Poplar" (profile area 5, 2020 Demographic Profiles); "Poplar" alone is not a City profile area name.

Where it sits: south of Highway 1, around Huntingdon Road, King Road and Gladwin Road, west of the Marshall Road / McCallum Road area and east toward Clearbrook Road. Highway 1 runs along the north edge with interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road; Huntingdon Road leads toward the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing via Highway 11 and Sumas Way; Highway 11 (Sumas Way) to the east connects Abbotsford to Mission.

Nearby areas: Clearbrook to the northwest, the City Centre / South Fraser Way corridor north across Highway 1, and Sumas Prairie to the east/southeast. Parks: Huntingdon Park, 34779 3rd Avenue, and Berry Park, 33928 Fern Street at the north edge. Transit: BC Transit routes 3 (Clearbrook / Huntingdon, via Gladwin and King Road), 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital, Marshall Road east edge), 6 (Gladwin Road corridor) and 12 (UFV / Bourquin via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride).

Schools physically inside the sub-area: South Poplar Traditional Elementary, 32746 Huntingdon Road; Jackson Elementary, 33165 King Road; Abbotsford Traditional School (middle and secondary), 2272 Windsor Street. SD34 catchments are address-based through the School Locator.

Civic anchors are outside the sub-area: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road, immediately north/northeast across Highway 1; Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way; Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Abbotsford Recreation Centre, 2499 McMillan Road. No shopping centre inside Poplar was verified on an official source.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Poplar

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: — RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²) in the urban north; A1 agricultural in the rural south (minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 ha where it applies). The zone section for the specific lot — not the sub-area name — decides subdivision, suite and added-unit questions.
OCP: Abbotsforward 2050 is CURRENT (adopted December 2025): No Poplar-specific neighbourhood plan is listed in the OCP.

SSMUH / added units on a lot: in June 2024 Council adopted Zoning Bylaw amendments implementing provincial small-scale multi-unit housing — June 2024 adoption is City-confirmed; the SSMUH bylaw NUMBER is UNCONFIRMED ("3560-2024" is asserted in some research material and must not be asserted — mark it UNCONFIRMED wherever met). Zoning Bylaw s.140 carries the small-scale rules and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, with City-report criteria including a lot of at least 400 m², at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — Abbotsford's rules ONLY.

ALR rules, where ALR ground exists (south edge): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal residence 500 m² or less; a secondary suite only within the principal residence; an additional residence capped at 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (parcels over 40 ha).

Strata block — background for any strata lot a Poplar search spills into: Form B (SPA s. 59) within 7 days of request, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, with the May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid age bylaw.

Market context, labelled community-level only: Abbotsford IS SnapStats-covered. September 2026, Poplar sub-area: detached inventory 27 / solds 2 (7%); condos & townhomes inventory 30 / solds 3 (10%) — a SMALL SAMPLE, no price conclusion drawn from it. Abbotsford community medians: detached $949,000; condos & townhomes $497,500. SnapStats has NO land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only) — no figure here is a land figure.

Poplar is named twice for the same ground, and only one name is the City's. The board calls it "Poplar"; the City's demographic profile calls the same ground "South Poplar" — and the community was named for the poplar trees planted on the top of the hill, with the Old South Poplar School on the Abbotsford Community Heritage Register. A search under only one name misses material filed under the other.
The September 2026 sub-area numbers are too thin to price land from.

Two Poplars, two servicing worlds. The same sub-area name covers serviced King Road subdivision lots and Huntingdon Road rural lots that may run on a well and a septic field — the single most consequential land check in Poplar is which side of that split a parcel sits on.

faq.q: What zoning and suite rules apply to a Poplar house lot?
faq.a: Urban lots use RS zones in Zoning Bylaw 2400-2014, with RS3 at a 540 m² minimum interior lot and RS5 at 420 m² in City reports, and one secondary suite permitted in all single detached dwellings under s.140.3.8, with City-stated criteria including a 400 m² minimum lot size and 12.0 m minimum frontage.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Poplar than in June?
faq.a: In Poplar, listings of houses fell from 28 in June to 27 in September (−3.6%); condos and townhomes rose from 18 in June to 30 in September (+66.7%).

faq.q: How big is Poplar compared with the rest of Abbotsford?
faq.a: In September 2026, Poplar held 6.1% of the 440 houses listed in Abbotsford and 5.2% of the 572 condos and townhomes listed in Abbotsford.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Poplar from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 9 houses and 17 condos and townhomes sold in Poplar over those 4 months.

faq.q: Can I actually buy a bare building lot in Poplar?
faq.a: Yes — but as an individual fee-simple parcel, not from a named bare-land subdivision: no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified for Poplar.

faq.q: How big are the lots, and can I split one?
faq.a: Zoning minimums are RS3 540 m² and RS5 420 m² for interior lots in the urban north, and 8.0 ha under A1 in the rural south — those are the floors a NEW lot must meet, so a purchase only has subdivision room if the parcel is comfortably larger than its zone minimum and meets frontage, road and servicing requirements through the Approving Officer. Most built Poplar lots sit at or near their minimum.

faq.q: Is a south-edge lot serviced, or will I need a well and septic?
faq.a: South-edge rural lots may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems — pull the GWELLS well record and the Fraser Health sewerage filings before offering, and confirm City connection status parcel by parcel: UNCONFIRMED for any single lot until those records are read.

faq.q: What extra units can go on a detached lot?
faq.a: One secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), subject to criteria including a 400 m² minimum lot and 12.0 m frontage; Abbotsford caps a suite at under 50% of the principal dwelling and a coach/garden suite at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m². The SSMUH bylaw number sometimes cited ("3560-2024") is UNCONFIRMED — do not rely on it.

faq.q: Is this lot in the ALR — and why does it matter?
faq.a: South-edge lots can be in or beside the ALR; check the parcel on the ALC map. If it is ALR, subdivision needs ALC approval, residences cannot be stratified, the A1 minimum is 8.0 ha, and the residence caps (principal 500 m²; suite inside the principal only; additional residence 90 m² / 186 m² by the 40 ha line) replace the urban rules.
